audit: Elliptic feature and label availability: primary-source review

sources.title: Anti-Money Laundering in Bitcoin: Experimenting with Graph Convolutional Networks for Financial Forensics
sources.short_quote: assuming the availability of ground truth after each time
sources.findings: 166 features comprise 94 local features including the time step and 72 one-hop backward/forward aggregates. The 49 time steps are approximately two weeks apart; each contains transactions within less than three hours. Its retrained-RF discussion assumes ground truth availability after each step; this is not an observed annotation timestamp.

sources.findings: Provider description counts the time-step field within the first 94 features; 72 additional features use one-hop backward/forward transaction information. Reviewed description provides no historical label-discovery timestamps.

sources.title: The enemy of reproducibility is opacity: What's inside the Elliptic bitcoin dataset (and why it is wrong)
sources.publication: Forensic Science International: Digital Investigation 57, 302124; June 2026 supplement

locations: Section 3.2, PDF page 4: fixed block 575059 and all available predecessor/successor neighbors
sources.short_quote: after the end of the test period
sources.findings: Authors report address-derived local features evaluated at dataset construction block 575059, later than the test period; neighbor aggregates also include transactions outside the released graph. They identify global z-score preprocessing and address reuse across temporal splits. Their reconstructed-feature agreement supports this criticism, but this audit did not reproduce the reconstruction. These findings materially strengthen the availability caveat; removing 72 neighbor aggregates does not remove future information from local features.

sources.authority: Paper authors, independently reconstructed semantics; not an Elliptic endorsement
locations: README Local transactions features derived from features of addresses: Features 23–94 at block 575059
sources.findings: Mapping specifies Feature 1 as time, Features 23–94 as address aggregates at the fixed reference block, and Features 95–166 as neighborhood aggregates. The mapping is reverse engineering, not original provider disclosure.

conclusions.statement: The official 94 local count includes one time-step field. Excluding time leaves 93 local predictors. Excluding time from 166 total leaves 165 predictors = 93 local + 72 aggregated. Publish the exact selected column indices; a 93-column vector is not the original 94-feature baseline.

Local-only does not imply available at transaction time. Delaying label release, splitting chronologically, or fitting a new scaler cannot erase future blockchain activity already encoded in provided vectors.

Use discrete step/batch replay. Within-step transaction arrival/order and feature readiness are not established by the public step field; txId ordering is not documented chronological order. Batch top-k decisions belong after batch completion.

Treat chosen label delays as scenario parameters. Neither reviewed official description nor original paper establishes historical label-discovery times; initial-history labels are an explicit availability assumption.

Keep Elliptic pilot as a retrospective benchmark/replay of precomputed features with simulated feedback availability. Do not claim causal live feature extraction, live transaction latency, leak-free detection or unseen-entity generalization. Hardware/queue/update implementation checks can still be meaningful within this stated scope.

A causal accuracy study needs time-scoped feature reconstruction or a separately justified feature set, suitable train-only preprocessing and an evaluation split matching the intended entity-generalization goal. Do not silently relabel a local-only ablation as repaired.

quote_policy: Each source has at most 25 quoted words; all other text is concise paraphrase/inference.
limitations: No raw Elliptic vectors or transaction reconstruction were downloaded or analyzed in this review.
The 2026 paper is a primary research claim, not a provider correction; cite attribution explicitly.
Absence of documented label timestamps is an availability limitation, not proof about investigators actual historical behavior.
